title: Heterogeneous-Requirement MAPE-K for Multimodal Reasoning Agents
research_question: Can a MAPE-K-style controller that optimizes heterogeneous requirements (accuracy, latency, and abstention risk) improve reliability of multimodal reasoning pipelines under distribution shift compared with static multimodal agent workflows?
hypothesis: Adapting the TUNE-style Bayesian model uncertainty mechanism and explicit heterogeneous requirement handling to multimodal reasoning agents will reduce overconfident failures and improve accuracy-latency trade-offs versus fixed orchestration policies.
motivation: The knowledge base shows a concrete open problem in self-adaptive systems: extending Bayesian model-uncertainty control to additional domains and heterogeneous requirements. At the same time, several nearby agentic workflow ideas have already been rejected in the KB, suggesting that another generic multi-agent orchestration proposal would likely lack novelty. A stronger gap is to transfer this validated self-adaptive control idea into multimodal reasoning, where models often fail under visual ambiguity and distribution shift, yet current workflows are typically static and optimize a single objective. This creates an opportunity for a cross-domain proposal: use MAPE-K plus Bayesian model averaging to decide when a multimodal pipeline should answer, defer, re-route, or invoke extra visual/textual evidence based on multiple runtime objectives.
